title: Boosting bottom-up milling of glass with GHz laser bursts
summary: Burst-mode laser processing has gained increasing attention in material machining due to its potential to enhance processing efficiency and quality. However, most studies have focused on conventional top-down machining strategies, while investigations of bottom-up milling (BUM) remain limited. In this work, we optimize processing parameters for high-efficiency glass milling using a bottom-up approach with GHz bursts. The results show that the highest BUM efficiencies are achieved when employing high pulse counts ($\geq$ 20). To the best of our knowledge, we report the highest glass milling efficiency, reaching more than 250 $μ$m$^3$/$μ$J for both soda-lime glass and fused silica. Furthermore, increasing the burst repetition rate while maintaining a parameter set associated with high milling efficiency enables a material removal rate larger than 8 mm$^3$/s.

title: Experimental Evidence of Cellular Sparing under Single-Pulse Picosecond Irradiation at Extreme Dose Rates
summary: Understanding how biological cells respond to radiation delivered on extremely short timescales is central to resolving the fundamental mechanisms underlying radiotherapy and to defining new regimes of radiobiology. This sparing effect is associated with a statistically significant reduction in the beta parameter of the linear-quadratic model, indicating reduced cell killing from accumulated sub-lethal damage. Picosecond irradiation also produced a marked reduction in prompt 53BP1 foci, but no significant difference in residual foci at 24h and foci-size distributions. These results provide the first experimental evidence of cellular sparing following single-pulse picosecond-scale irradiation. Direct comparison with recent work at femtosecond timescales suggests the presence of a previously undetected sharp transition in biological response at the femtosecond/picosecond interface, giving critical insight on the possible mechanisms responsible for this differential response.

title: Hydrograd v2.0: a differentiable two-dimensional shallow-water model on unstructured meshes with steady and unsteady adjoints for calibration and closure learning
summary: We present \textit{Hydrograd} v2.0, a significantly improved differentiable 2D shallow-water model written in Python with JAX. The model solves the shallow-water equations on the unstructured meshes of production models such as SRH-2D and HEC-RAS 2D with a well-balanced, positivity-preserving finite-volume scheme that handles wetting and drying. Gradients are tailored to the type of problem. Steady states are found by Newton's method with an exact sparse Jacobian obtained by graph colouring, and their gradients follow from the implicit function theorem at the cost of one linear solve. Unsteady flows are differentiated in reverse mode with checkpointing, or with an implicit time integrator whose gradient costs about two forward runs. All gradients agree with finite differences, to about $10^{-8}$ for steady flows. On the Savannah River case, the steady water surface differs from that of SRH-2D by 4.7\,mm (root mean square). Steady closure learning was 96 times faster than differentiating through time marching and reached a lower loss. An inflow hydrograph was inverted from stage records with a peak error of 2\,\%. In an unsteady roughness calibration, a singular value decomposition analysis of the sensitivity matrix showed that the stage records at the gauges are 70 to 160 times more sensitive to the total resistance of the reach than to its distribution among the roughness zones, which explains why only a gauge layout with gauges in every zone recovered all five roughness values. On one GPU, a mesh of 512,000 cells takes 7.6\,s for a forward run and 51\,s for a gradient.

title: Parametric spatio-temporal reduced-order modelling via Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and Gaussian Process Regression
summary: We present SPOD-GPR, a non-intrusive, parametric, spatio-temporal reduced-order model (ROM) that combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), Spectral POD (SPOD), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). A parametric POD first projects the high-dimensional state onto a low-dimensional subspace. The reduced trajectories are then divided into windowed sections, transformed into the frequency domain, and truncated to the most energetic frequencies. SPOD is then performed independently at each retained frequency, yielding temporally coherent modes and coefficients. The parametric dependence of the POD and SPOD bases is modelled by GPR on a local chart of the Grassmann manifold after Procrustes alignment. The SPOD modal coefficients are learned both as explicit functions of the parameters and through a parameter-conditioned autoregressive model that allows for temporal extrapolation beyond the training window. Gaussian processes are sampled jointly and pathwise via Matheron conditioning, ensuring that each predictive realization carries uncertainty quantification consistent with the posterior distribution. The method is tested on four parametric examples where the parameter values and the prediction horizon lie outside the training data: the two-dimensional anisotropic Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equation in a time-periodic and a travelling-wave regime, each parametrised by one of its two coefficients; flow past a cylinder parametrised by the Reynolds number; and flow past an elliptic obstacle parametrised by its semi-axes. In all cases, SPOD-GPR reduces the normalised mean absolute error compared to a POD-GPR baseline, and improves the calibration of the predictive uncertainty, especially in the fluid flow cases, where POD-GPR is severely overconfident. This opens the way to spectral, uncertainty-aware reduced-order models for many-query and real-time applications, such as digital twins.

title: Optical frequency combs on thin-film lithium niobate: from principles to applications

summary: Optical frequency combs, consisting of mutually coherent and equally spaced spectral lines, provide a powerful means of synthesizing, distributing, and processing optical frequencies on chip. title: Magnetized plasma modulator for polarization-tunable ultrahigh-power single-cycle lasers
summary: Ultrahigh power lasers with tunable polarization and few-cycle duration have long been considered the holy grail of high-power laser science, as they push light-matter interactions into an entirely new physical regime. Yet such pulses remain far beyond the reach of conventional solid-state optics and technologies. Here, we introduce a novel magnetized plasma modulator that boosts linearly polarized lasers from petawatt to exawatt powers while simultaneously enabling tunable polarization, offering a promising approach for high-power laser development. This is achieved in density-tailored plasmas by combining dispersive compression of a chirped picosecond laser pulse with magneto-chiral group-velocity splitting in a few-Tesla magnetic field. It can generate circularly or elliptically polarized pulses with extremely high compression ratios (over 1000) and extremely short durations (down to the single-cycle level) in a compact and efficient manner. These findings demonstrate a feasible pathway toward exawatt-class few-cycle lasers with tunable polarization, opening new avenues for a wide range of cutting-edge research and applications.

AI.motivation: Ultrahigh-power few-cycle lasers with tunable polarization are highly desirable for accessing new light-matter interaction regimes, but conventional solid-state optics and technologies cannot provide such pulses.

title: Universal Approximation by Equivariant Message-Passing Graph Neural Networks with a Bilinear Readout
summary: We prove universal approximation for the bilinear-readout equivariant message-passing network (BREMP), a reference architecture for equivariant graph neural network interatomic potentials. Its layers combine equivariant convolutions with affine maps, and its readout forms invariants from products of the equivariant features. We construct a one-layer feature that determines the local environment up to permutations of atoms of the same type. The construction uses spherical harmonic filters of degree no larger than the largest number of neighbors at a common distance from the center. Iterating the construction recovers the environment reachable in as many hops as there are layers, using the same bound on filter degrees at the layer cutoff. The readout approximates every continuous invariant function of the features uniformly on compact sets. Together these give universal approximation of atomic energies at a prescribed physical range using a shorter layer cutoff. We assume that, throughout the admissible class, message passing reaches all neighbors in each physical environment within a common number of layers. Finally, DPA4, an interatomic potential architecture in production use, inherits this result by approximating the BREMP layers constructed in the proof and realizing the bilinear readout.

title: Phase-resolved turbulence dynamics in cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsatile pipe flow
comment: 37 pages, 20 figures, 2 tables. Includes 3 supplementary movies. Submitted to Journal of Fluid Mechanics
summary: Direct numerical simulations examine the phase-dependent turbulence dynamics of pipe flow driven by cardiac-cycle-inspired waveforms. Four cases with and without a low-flow plateau span two Reynolds-number ranges. The response follows four stages of turbulent--turbulent reorganisation. Strong acceleration suppresses transverse fluctuations and vortical activity. During acceleration and early deceleration, streamwise-normal-stress production recovers ahead of pressure--strain redistribution and radial momentum transport, allowing energy to accumulate in elongated streaks. In early deceleration, near-wall high-speed streaks develop predominantly varicose disturbances associated with Q4 sweeps, whereas outer-buffer-layer low-speed streaks develop predominantly sinuous disturbances associated with Q2 ejections. The transition exhibits distinct radial sequences: Q2-based local onset occurs progressively later towards the wall, whereas Q4-based onset is nearly simultaneous across the viscous sublayer and buffer layer, with peaks occurring successively outwards. The two responses overlap between the drag minimum and recovery maximum as redistribution intensifies markedly and multiscale momentum transport recovers rapidly. Turbulence then decays and its scales readjust. Where present, the plateau prolongs this decay and weakens the turbulence inherited by the next acceleration stage. It further delays local instability and lengthens the onset-to-peak intervals of the shear contributions. An unsteady friction decomposition links these phase-dependent dynamics to the drag response, highlighting the role of delayed turbulent shear recovery in sustaining the low-drag interval.

The two responses overlap between the drag minimum and recovery maximum as redistribution intensifies and multiscale momentum transport recovers rapidly. Turbulence then decays and its scales readjust. Where present, the plateau prolongs decay, weakens turbulence inherited by the next acceleration stage, delays local instability, and lengthens onset-to-peak intervals of shear contributions. The unsteady friction decomposition links these dynamics to drag, highlighting delayed turbulent shear recovery in sustaining the low-drag interval.
AI.conclusion: Phase-resolved turbulent–turbulent reorganisation under cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsatile pipe flow is governed by distinct acceleration, deceleration, overlap, and decay stages, with streak-type disturbances and radial onset sequences depending on flow phase. A low-flow plateau extends decay and reduces turbulence inherited by the next acceleration, and delayed turbulent shear recovery helps sustain the low-drag interval.

title: Off-focus detection for SNR enhancement in coherent single-pixel imaging
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures; supplementary material (9 pages) included as ancillary file
summary: Coherent single-pixel imaging (CSPI) enables amplitude- and phase-resolved computational imaging with a single coherent detector, offering particular advantages in spectral regimes where high-performance detector arrays remain unavailable. In conventional Fourier-plane CSPI, the detector is typically placed at the focal point to maximize the collected power. However, this focal position does not necessarily maximize the reconstruction fidelity for image reconstruction in the presence of system nonidealities. Here, we introduce detector position as an additional degree of freedom for CSPI optimization. We show that appropriately selected off-focus Fourier-plane positions can improve reconstruction performance by suppressing fluctuation-sensitive coherent backgrounds while preserving spatially encoded signals. Experimentally, using a programmable liquid-crystal terahertz spatial light modulator and coherent heterodyne detection, we demonstrate improved amplitude and phase reconstruction from selected off-focus channels compared with focal detection. A symmetric off-focus pair with complementary transverse-wave-vector weighting further enhances image fidelity, contrast, and compressive-sampling robustness through coherent channel fusion. These results establish detector-position engineering as a new strategy for enhancing the robustness and information efficiency of CSPI.

The authors therefore seek an additional optimization degree of freedom to enhance reconstruction performance and signal-to-noise ratio.

title: Heterogeneous Acceleration of TRIMEG++ code using OpenMP for Gyrokinetic Simulations
summary: Turbulent transport largely determines the performance of magnetic-confinement fusion devices such as tokamaks, and gyrokinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations are a principal tool to predict it. Advancing up to hundreds of millions of markers and solving large sparse field systems at every time step makes whole-device simulations among the most expensive in plasma physics. GPUs can accelerate this workload, but porting a complex code requires restructuring its parallelism and memory traffic, ideally without a separate version per vendor. In this work, the gyrokinetic code TRIMEG-C1, whose unstructured triangular mesh and high-order finite elements cover both the confined core and the open-field-line edge of the plasma, is rewritten in C++ as TRIMEG++ and fully offloaded to GPUs with OpenMP target directives, so that one portable code base runs on both AMD and NVIDIA hardware. The particle-to-grid projection is offloaded in its standard and field-aligned formulations, the PETSc-based field solver runs on the GPU through the library's backends, and, together with the previously offloaded particle pusher, every stage whose cost scales with the marker count runs on the GPU. All speedups are node-to-node comparisons against a 256-core CPU node (2x AMD EPYC 9754). On the TCV-X21 tokamak reference case, the offloaded kernels reproduce the CPU results to a relative accuracy of 1e-11, and the full simulation runs 4.1-6.1x faster on a node with two AMD MI300A and 2.1-3.0x faster on a node with four NVIDIA A100, with the speedup growing with problem size. The MI300A, with shared CPU-GPU memory, needs no explicit data transfers, whereas the A100 needs them managed by hand. These results show that directive-based offloading can accelerate a complex gyrokinetic code across GPU vendors, making whole-volume tokamak simulations with hundreds of millions of markers practical on a single GPU node.

AI.tldr: TRIMEG++ is a C++ rewrite of the gyrokinetic particle-in-cell code TRIMEG-C1, fully offloaded to AMD and NVIDIA GPUs using portable OpenMP target directives and validated on a TCV-X21 tokamak case with 1e-11 relative accuracy and 2.1-6.1x node-to-node speedups.
AI.motivation: Turbulent transport strongly affects magnetic-confinement fusion performance, and gyrokinetic particle-in-cell simulations are a principal prediction tool, but whole-device simulations with hundreds of millions of markers and large sparse field solves are extremely expensive. GPUs can accelerate this workload, yet porting a complex code requires restructuring parallelism and memory traffic while avoiding separate vendor-specific versions.

Speedups were measured node-to-node against a 256-core CPU node with two AMD EPYC 9754 processors.
AI.result: On the TCV-X21 tokamak reference case, the offloaded kernels reproduced CPU results to 1e-11 relative accuracy. The full simulation ran 4.1-6.1x faster on a node with two AMD MI300A GPUs and 2.1-3.0x faster on a node with four NVIDIA A100 GPUs, with speedup increasing with problem size. MI300A shared CPU-GPU memory required no explicit data transfers, whereas A100 transfers were managed by hand.
AI.conclusion: Directive-based GPU offloading can accelerate a complex gyrokinetic code across GPU vendors, making whole-volume tokamak simulations with hundreds of millions of markers practical on a single GPU node.

title: Elastic frontogenesis sets the spectra of smooth elastic turbulence
summary: Most turbulent flows are sustained by inertia, which transfers energy across scales and produces characteristic power-law spectra. Yet dilute polymer solutions also exhibit turbulence when inertia is negligible: in this state, known as elastic turbulence, the velocity field remains spatially smooth while both the velocity and the polymer conformation exhibit robust power-law spectra. How a smooth flow, lacking a hierarchy of eddies, generates such multiscale structure has remained unexplained. Here we show that the missing mechanism is elastic frontogenesis, whereby the flow spontaneously organizes polymer stress into thin sheets that are stretched within their plane and compressed across their thickness, causing their amplitude to grow as they become thinner. Because the fronts are sheet-like structures, this amplification-thinning law uniquely determines the polymer conformation spectrum, while the Stokes response transfers the same geometric scaling to the velocity field, reconciling broadband spectra with spatial smoothness. Being geometric rather than model-specific, elastic frontogenesis provides an organizing principle for viscoelastic flows and the viscoelastic analogue of vortex stretching in inertial turbulence.

AI.tldr: Elastic frontogenesis explains how elastic turbulence can produce robust power-law velocity and polymer-conformation spectra while the velocity field remains spatially smooth.
AI.motivation: Dilute polymer solutions exhibit elastic turbulence when inertia is negligible, producing power-law spectra despite a spatially smooth velocity field. The mechanism by which a smooth flow without a hierarchy of eddies generates multiscale structure was unexplained.
AI.method: The abstract proposes a mechanistic explanation based on elastic frontogenesis: polymer stress spontaneously organizes into thin sheets that are stretched in-plane and compressed across their thickness. It invokes an amplification-thinning law and a Stokes response linking polymer-stress geometry to the velocity field. Specific experimental, numerical, or theoretical methods are not provided in the abstract.
AI.result: The sheet-like fronts grow in amplitude as they thin, and this amplification-thinning law uniquely determines the polymer conformation spectrum. The Stokes response transfers the same geometric scaling to the velocity field, reconciling broadband power-law spectra with spatial smoothness.
AI.conclusion: Elastic frontogenesis is proposed as a geometric organizing principle for viscoelastic flows and as the viscoelastic analogue of vortex stretching in inertial turbulence.

title: X-ray parametric down-conversion probes radiation-induced dynamics in hybrid perovskite MAPbBr3
summary: We report minute-timescale time-resolved measurements of X-ray parametric down-conversion (PDC) of X-rays into ultraviolet photons in a MAPbBr3 single crystal under continuous irradiation. Despite the known radiation sensitivity of hybrid perovskites and the high photon flux required to detect the intrinsically weak PDC signal, the nonlinear response remains measurable throughout the irradiation sequence. Both PDC and Bragg diffraction exhibit a slow decay consistent with diffusion-driven damage dynamics on timescales reported for bromide-vacancy and proton migration. However, despite their similar decay rates, the PDC and Bragg signals evolve toward markedly different steady states, while an additional fast decay component is observed in the Bragg response but absent in the PDC signal. Density functional theory calculations identify N 2s states of the methylammonium cation as the most likely contributors to the measured PDC response and show that their Fourier component is only weakly affected by bromide-vacancy formation. These results establish nonlinear X-ray diffraction as a channel-selective probe of radiation-induced dynamics and demonstrate that radiation damage can couple differently to nonlinear and linear X-ray responses.

AI.tldr: Minute-timescale X-ray parametric down-conversion (PDC) measurements in a MAPbBr3 single crystal under continuous irradiation show that the nonlinear PDC response remains measurable despite radiation-sensitive damage, decays similarly to Bragg diffraction but reaches a different steady state and lacks the fast Bragg decay component; DFT attributes the PDC response mainly to methylammonium N 2s states weakly affected by bromide vacancies.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to probe radiation-induced dynamics in hybrid perovskites and to test whether nonlinear X-ray diffraction, specifically X-ray parametric down-conversion, responds differently from linear Bragg diffraction to radiation damage. It is motivated by the known radiation sensitivity of hybrid perovskites and the challenge of measuring intrinsically weak PDC under high photon flux.
AI.method: Time-resolved, minute-timescale measurements of X-ray parametric down-conversion of X-rays into ultraviolet photons were performed in a MAPbBr3 single crystal under continuous irradiation. The PDC response was compared with Bragg diffraction, and density functional theory calculations were used to identify atomic states contributing to the measured PDC response and their sensitivity to bromide-vacancy formation.

Both PDC and Bragg diffraction showed a slow decay consistent with diffusion-driven damage dynamics on timescales reported for bromide-vacancy and proton migration, but they evolved toward markedly different steady states. A fast decay component appeared in Bragg diffraction but was absent in PDC. DFT identified N 2s states of the methylammonium cation as the most likely contributors to the PDC response and showed that their Fourier component is only weakly affected by bromide-vacancy formation.

title: A Mathematical Multiscale Framework for Nonlinear Modeling of the Heliosphere
summary: The inner heliosphere is a highly nonlinear continuous medium where macroscopic ideal magnetohydrodynamics is inextricably coupled with microscopic, fully developed stochastic turbulence. State-of-the-art global 3D numerical solvers, while proficient at capturing the large-scale propagation of extreme space physics phenomena such as coronal mass ejections and corotating interaction regions, are computationally constrained by grid resolution and fundamental partial differential equation formulations. Consequently, they inherently do not resolve the local small-scale turbulent cascade, magnetic intermittency, and localized thermodynamic anomalies. To bridge this fundamental scaleseparation gap, this paper presents a novel mathematical and numerical framework that harmoniously integrates global heliospheric structures with local turbulent physics. The framework generates a highly realistic synthetic continuous medium by superimposing a stochastically driven nonlinear turbulent cascade onto a bimodal deterministic background flow. This cascade reproduces theoretical constraints for fractional power spectral densities, magnetic compressibility, and small-scale intermittency via a discrete multiplicative binomial cascade (p-model). This multiscale continuous background is dynamically perturbed by analytical models of large-scale nonlinear transients, including kinematic shock steepening, continuous current sheet topological reversals, and solar ejecta formalized as asymmetric force-free magnetic flux ropes. By generating exact spatio-temporal arrays across arbitrary distributed coordinates, this unified mathematical model overcomes the spatial degeneracy of single-point observations and provides a computationally efficient analytical baseline for performance models supporting future in-situ multi-spacecraft heliospheric missions, which are currently in their feasibility study phase.

AI.tldr: Presents a mathematical and numerical multiscale framework that superimposes a stochastic nonlinear turbulent cascade on a bimodal deterministic heliospheric background and adds analytical transient models, generating realistic synthetic continuous-medium fields for future multi-spacecraft heliospheric mission studies.
AI.motivation: Global 3D magnetohydrodynamic solvers capture large-scale heliospheric phenomena such as coronal mass ejections and corotating interaction regions, but grid resolution and partial differential equation formulations prevent them from resolving small-scale turbulent cascades, magnetic intermittency, and localized thermodynamic anomalies. A framework is needed to bridge this fundamental scale separation.
AI.method: The framework integrates global heliospheric structures with local turbulent physics by superimposing a stochastically driven nonlinear turbulent cascade, implemented as a discrete multiplicative binomial cascade (p-model), onto a bimodal deterministic background flow. The cascade reproduces constraints on fractional power spectral densities, magnetic compressibility, and small-scale intermittency. Analytical models then perturb this background with kinematic shock steepening, continuous current sheet topological reversals, and solar ejecta represented as asymmetric force-free magnetic flux ropes. Exact spatio-temporal arrays are generated at arbitrary distributed coordinates.
AI.result: The framework produces a highly realistic synthetic continuous medium, overcomes the spatial degeneracy of single-point observations, and provides a computationally efficient analytical baseline for performance models supporting future in-situ multi-spacecraft heliospheric missions currently in feasibility study. The abstract reports no quantitative validation or performance results.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that a unified multiscale mathematical and numerical framework can harmoniously integrate global heliospheric structures with local turbulent physics, providing a computationally efficient analytical baseline for future multi-spacecraft heliospheric mission performance modeling.

title: Velocity gradient tensor reconstruction from tracer orientations via Jeffery dynamics
summary: The velocity gradient tensor is a local quantity, but methods that obtain it by spatial differencing of the velocities of spherical tracers amplify measurement noise. We propose a method that reconstructs the velocity gradient tensor from the orientations of non-spherical tracers such as flakes and rods. Based on the Jeffery-type equation, we show that, for incompressible flow, all components of the velocity gradient tensor are uniquely determined from the orientations of four tracers and their time derivatives in the neighbourhood of a reference point (orientation-based method). The method uses neither tracer positions nor spatial differencing. It therefore requires orientation measurements only near the reference point, without requiring measurements throughout a three-dimensional region, and measurement noise is amplified only through temporal differencing. Consequently, the minimum achievable error scales as $σ^{1/2}$ with the noise level $σ$, compared with $σ^{1/3}$ for the positional PTV-plus-differencing approach (position-based method). Numerical tests further show that the vorticity is reconstructed more accurately than by the position-based method, whereas the strain rate is reconstructed with comparable accuracy. Finally, applying the method to spherical Couette flow, we find that the reconstruction fails where the neighbouring tracers align, which renders the inversion ill-conditioned, and that this degeneracy appears as the characteristic light-and-dark pattern familiar from flow visualization.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an orientation-based method that reconstructs the velocity gradient tensor from the orientations and time derivatives of four non-spherical tracers using Jeffery dynamics in incompressible flow, avoiding tracer positions and spatial differencing. It achieves a minimum error scaling of σ^(1/2) versus σ^(1/3) for position-based PTV-plus-differencing, reconstructs vorticity more accurately and strain rate comparably, but fails where neighbouring tracers align and the inversion becomes ill-conditioned.
AI.motivation: Obtaining the velocity gradient tensor by spatially differencing the velocities of spherical tracers amplifies measurement noise, motivating an alternative that does not rely on tracer positions or spatial differencing.
AI.method: Based on the Jeffery-type equation, the authors show that for incompressible flow all components of the velocity gradient tensor are uniquely determined from the orientations of four tracers and their time derivatives in the neighbourhood of a reference point. The orientation-based method uses neither tracer positions nor spatial differencing, requires orientation measurements only near the reference point rather than throughout a three-dimensional region, and amplifies measurement noise only through temporal differencing.
AI.result: The minimum achievable error scales as σ^(1/2) with noise level σ, compared with σ^(1/3) for the positional PTV-plus-differencing approach. Numerical tests show that vorticity is reconstructed more accurately than by the position-based method, while strain rate is reconstructed with comparable accuracy. In spherical Couette flow, reconstruction fails where neighbouring tracers align, making the inversion ill-conditioned; this degeneracy appears as the characteristic light-and-dark pattern familiar from flow visualization.
AI.conclusion: Reconstructing the velocity gradient tensor from non-spherical tracer orientations via Jeffery dynamics is a viable alternative to position-based spatial differencing, offering improved vorticity accuracy and comparable strain-rate accuracy, but its accuracy is limited by ill-conditioning when neighbouring tracers align.

title: Tunable Near-Unity Light Absorption via Surface Exciton-Polaritons in Periodic Gratings of Anisotropic Polarizable Materials
comment: Accepted for publication in Journal of Physics Condensed Matter
summary: Near-perfect light absorption in ultrathin films is hindered by two fundamental obstacles: the momentum mismatch that prevents resonant excitation of surface exciton-polaritons (SEPs) under ordinary illumination, and the 50% absorption ceiling imposed on free-standing conductive sheets by geometric symmetry. Here we show that both obstacles can be overcome simultaneously in a simple, planar geometry. A one-dimensional periodic grating of anisotropic polarizable ribbons composed of J-aggregates supporting bright molecular excitons provides the reciprocal lattice momentum needed to excite SEPs without employing an attenuated total reflection configuration, while a metallic mirror beneath a dielectric spacer folds the reflected field back onto the absorber, breaking the $50\%$ limit through interference between the incident and reflected waves. We develop a semi-analytical matrix formulation to compute the full optical response of such structure, and demonstrate that the absorptance at the first-order SEP resonance can be continuously tuned from near-unity to near-zero by varying the spacer thickness alone. The grating period and filling factor offer additional spectral control, and oblique incidence unlocks a second, out-of-plane polariton branch. These results establish periodic gratings of excitonic media as a versatile, practical and integrable platform for spectrally selective, near-perfect light absorption.

AI.tldr: A planar grating of anisotropic J-aggregate ribbons over a dielectric spacer and metallic mirror enables grating-coupled surface exciton-polariton excitation and interference-enhanced near-unity absorption that is tunable through spacer thickness.
AI.motivation: Ultrathin-film near-perfect absorption is limited by momentum mismatch for surface exciton-polariton excitation under ordinary illumination and by the 50% absorption ceiling of free-standing conductive sheets imposed by geometric symmetry.
AI.method: The authors use a one-dimensional periodic grating of anisotropic polarizable J-aggregate ribbons supporting bright molecular excitons to supply reciprocal lattice momentum, with a metallic mirror beneath a dielectric spacer to fold the reflected field back onto the absorber. They develop a semi-analytical matrix formulation to compute the full optical response and examine spacer thickness, grating period, filling factor, and oblique incidence.
AI.result: The absorptance at the first-order surface exciton-polariton resonance can be continuously tuned from near-unity to near-zero by varying only the spacer thickness. Grating period and filling factor provide additional spectral control, and oblique incidence enables a second, out-of-plane polariton branch.
AI.conclusion: Periodic gratings of excitonic media are established as a versatile, practical, and integrable platform for spectrally selective, near-perfect light absorption.

title: Regulating pedestal pressure profile by microtearing modes in the EAST tokamak
summary: The pedestal pressure profile plays a critical role in determining the overall confinement of tokamak fusion plasmas. This letter reports the first evidence on regulating pedestal pressure profile by microtearing modes (MTMs) via limiting the pedestal gradient, which was thought to be limited by kinetic ballooning modes over the last decades. This is observed in an ITER-baseline-like target plasma in the EAST tokamak. MTMs arrest the recovery of pedestal electron temperature (and hence pressure) by clamping its gradient at a critical value while leaving the density profile essentially unaffected. Global fluid and local gyrokinetic simulations confirm the excitation of MTMs when the pedestal electron temperature gradient exceeds a threshold value in this experiment. This finding reveals MTMs as an alternative electromagnetic micro-instability that imposes an additional constraint in determining the pedestal structure in tokamaks.

AI.tldr: In EAST tokamak ITER-baseline-like plasmas, microtearing modes are observed for the first time to regulate the pedestal pressure profile by clamping the pedestal electron-temperature gradient at a critical value, with density largely unaffected; global fluid and local gyrokinetic simulations support MTM excitation above a threshold gradient.
AI.motivation: The pedestal pressure profile critically determines overall confinement in tokamak fusion plasmas. For decades, pedestal gradients were thought to be limited primarily by kinetic ballooning modes, so the study tests whether another electromagnetic micro-instability can regulate pedestal structure.
AI.method: The authors analyze an ITER-baseline-like target plasma in the EAST tokamak and report experimental evidence of pedestal regulation by microtearing modes. They use global fluid simulations and local gyrokinetic simulations to confirm MTM excitation when the pedestal electron-temperature gradient exceeds a threshold value.
AI.result: MTMs arrest the recovery of pedestal electron temperature and hence pressure by clamping its gradient at a critical value, while leaving the density profile essentially unaffected. Simulations confirm MTM excitation above the measured threshold electron-temperature gradient.
AI.conclusion: Microtearing modes are identified as an alternative electromagnetic micro-instability that imposes an additional constraint on pedestal structure in tokamaks, challenging the longstanding view that kinetic ballooning modes alone limit the pedestal gradient.

title: Thermochemical Rossby waves in rapid rotation: from swallowtail geometry to nonlinear selection
summary: When heat and solute both destabilise a rapidly rotating fluid, do their buoyancies add? Codensity models assume so, giving a straight onset diagonal; spherical shells show curved and kinked thresholds. We study the Busse--Simitev rotating annulus, whose normal modes obey an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. Combining the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope yields, in the rapid-rotation limit, an explicit swallowtail wave front, in Arnold's sense, that bends the codensity diagonal into smooth and then kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases. Its cusp edges lie inside the unstable domain and its exposed kink ends at the swallowtail singularity; these are singularities of wave-number selection, without coalescence of temporal eigenvalues, and the swallowtail diffusivity ratio has analytical small- and large-Prandtl-number limits. At a kink, broad, fast thermal and narrow, slow compositional Rossby waves become neutral together; hidden arcs mark the birth and merger of unstable wave-number bands. The same geometry enters nonlinear selection: mean-scalar feedback factors through neutral-arc normals and scalar responses, so the mean-profile coexistence margin vanishes with the kink angle as the waves merge. Complete cubic coefficients predict robust coexistence at a reference corner and a narrow bistable interval near merger. Exact finite-rotation corners and periodic-cell simulations confirm the coexisting waves and their invasion thresholds.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes thermochemical Rossby-wave onset and nonlinear selection in the rapidly rotating Busse–Simitev annulus using an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. Combining the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope produces an explicit swallowtail wave front that bends the codensity onset diagonal into smooth and kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases; the same geometry controls mean-scalar feedback and wave coexistence.
AI.motivation: Codensity models assume that thermal and compositional buoyancies simply add, yielding a straight onset diagonal, whereas spherical-shell calculations show curved and kinked thresholds. The paper aims to explain this discrepancy and determine how the resulting wave geometry affects nonlinear selection and coexistence.
AI.method: The authors study the Busse–Simitev rotating annulus, whose normal modes satisfy an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. They combine the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope in the rapid-rotation limit, analyze the resulting swallowtail geometry in Arnold’s sense, derive analytical small- and large-Prandtl-number limits of the swallowtail diffusivity ratio, and use complete cubic coefficients, exact finite-rotation corners, and periodic-cell simulations to assess nonlinear selection.
AI.result: The analysis yields an explicit swallowtail wave front that bends the codensity diagonal into smooth and then kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases. Cusp edges lie inside the unstable domain, and the exposed kink terminates at the swallowtail singularity, corresponding to wave-number-selection singularities without temporal-eigenvalue coalescence. At a kink, broad fast thermal and narrow slow compositional Rossby waves become neutral together, with hidden arcs marking birth and merger of unstable wave-number bands. Mean-scalar feedback acts through neutral-arc normals and scalar responses, causing the mean-profile coexistence margin to vanish with the kink angle. Cubic coefficients predict robust coexistence at a reference corner and a narrow bistable interval near merger; finite-rotation corners and periodic-cell simulations confirm the coexisting waves and invasion thresholds.
AI.conclusion: Thermal and compositional buoyancies do not generally combine according to a simple codensity diagonal under rapid rotation. Instead, their interaction produces a swallowtail onset geometry whose kinks govern wave-number selection and nonlinear coexistence, with the coexistence margin disappearing as the thermal and compositional Rossby waves merge.

title: Silicon and silicon nitride photonic ring resonator arrays for photonic trimming metrology
comment: Acknowledgement of Canadian Microsystems Passive Silicon Photonics Fabrication Workshop (CMC SiEPIC)
summary: Proposed silicon on silicon oxide 4x4 matrix multiplier for use in refractive index measurements, based on the Advanced Micro Foundry deep ultraviolet process. Agreement between simulated spectra and analytic design spectra demonstrate the intended performance of the components given a 1550 nm wavelength spectrum analysis. AI.method: A 4×4 matrix multiplier on silicon-on-silicon oxide was designed using Advanced Micro Foundry's deep ultraviolet process. Simulated spectra were compared with analytic design spectra at 1550 nm, and the design was assessed for cladding optical damage analysis and refractive-index analysis after sub-threshold laser ablation; femtosecond multi-shot refractive-index tuning was also evaluated.

title: Analysis of Solid Boron Injection for ITER
summary: Since ITER will now operate with a full tungsten divertor and first wall, the ITER Organization is considering boron wall conditioning schemes to getter oxygen and reduce tungsten sputtering to avoid excessive radiation to ensure that ITER can reach and sustain high- performance plasma operation. ITER has adopted Glow Discharge Boronization (GDB) in deuterated diborane (B$_2$D$_6$) as its main technique, which can only be performed in the absence of magnetic fields, but has also requested a study to determine how effective solid boron injection (SBI), which can be performed during plasma operation, using either an Impurity Powder Dropper (IPD) or a boron pellet injector, might be as a risk mitigation to achieving Q=10. Solid impurity injection has been used for decades as a wall conditioning technique on numerous tokamaks and stellarators around the world. The study presented here begins to assess SBI on ITER by first quantifying the boron source term across a particle size scan from 1 $μ$m to 5 mm diameter and an injection velocity scan from 5 -- 200 m/s for several ITER plasma conditions: 1) Start of Research Operations (SRO) diverted L-mode, 2) Q=10 H-mode, and 3) low plasma current and low power limiter operation. Modeling of the ablation, transport, erosion and redeposition of solid boron is being carried out with the Dust Injection Simulator (DIS), the Neutral Gas Shielding (NGS), EMC3-EIRENE and WallDYN3D models. In the first steps presented here, the DIS and NGS models are compared for calculating the boron source term that is then used as input to EMC3-EIRENE and will later be used with WallDYN3D.

AI.tldr: Initial modeling assesses solid boron injection as an in-operation wall-conditioning risk mitigation for ITER, comparing dust-injection and neutral-gas-shielding source-term models across particle sizes, injection velocities, and three plasma scenarios.
AI.motivation: ITER will operate with a full tungsten divertor and first wall, so boron wall conditioning is being considered to getter oxygen and reduce tungsten sputtering, thereby avoiding excessive radiation and supporting high-performance plasma operation. Glow Discharge Boronization is the main technique but can only be used without magnetic fields; solid boron injection could be performed during plasma operation and is therefore being evaluated as a risk mitigation for achieving Q=10.
AI.method: The study quantifies the solid boron source term over a particle diameter scan from 1 μm to 5 mm and an injection velocity scan from 5 to 200 m/s for three ITER plasma conditions: Start of Research Operations diverted L-mode, Q=10 H-mode, and low plasma current and low power limiter operation. Ablation, transport, erosion, and redeposition modeling uses the Dust Injection Simulator, Neutral Gas Shielding, EMC3-EIRENE, and WallDYN3D models; in the first steps, DIS and NGS are compared for calculating the boron source term used as input to EMC3-EIRENE and later to WallDYN3D.
AI.result: The abstract reports the beginning of an assessment of solid boron injection for ITER and a comparison of the DIS and NGS models for calculating the boron source term across the specified particle size, velocity, and plasma-condition scans. No quantitative results are provided in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Solid boron injection is being evaluated as a possible risk mitigation for achieving Q=10 in ITER because it can be performed during plasma operation, unlike Glow Discharge Boronization. The presented work establishes initial source-term modeling steps, with EMC3-EIRENE and later WallDYN3D analyses planned; the abstract does not provide final effectiveness conclusions.

title: Flash evaporation Riemann Problem: Thermodynamic Relaxation and Oscillation-Free Real Fluid Finite Volume Method
summary: The Flash evaporation Riemann problem (FeRP) formulated the wave structures of flash evaporation in the vapor-liquid homogeneous equilibrium limit. However, physical flash evaporation involves finite-rate interphase heat and mass transfer, inducing the wave structure to deviate from the equilibrium state. To solve such a non-equilibrium Riemann problem, this paper first derives the governing equation of mechanical equilibrium evolution in a relaxation system, based on which an oscillation-free Homogeneous Relaxation Real Fluid (HRRF) finite volume method is developed. In addition to the Euler equations with mass relaxation, the HRRF method evolves advection equations for the internal energy--pressure affine parameters and the vapor volume fraction, in order to eliminate numerical pressure oscillations inherent in conservative methods while preserving phase-transition-induced pressure changes, and consistently degenerate into a completely pressure-equilibrium method in supercritical flows. The HRRF method is then employed to comprehensively evaluate how thermodynamic relaxation affects the FeRP solution. Results indicate that the non-classical expansion shock of the FeRP loses its traveling-wave characteristics with increasing relaxation time, continuously degenerating into a self-similar rarefaction wave. Compared with the equilibrium limit, an increased mass transfer relaxation time smooths the expansion branch of the RP solution, lowers the intermediate pressure and velocity, and induces a pseudo-splitting of the rarefaction wave as well as a pseudo-advance of the phase transition onset. Meanwhile, the heat transfer relaxation time primarily dictates the temperature difference in the vapor-liquid mixture, thereby modulating the liquid superheat and in turn influencing the mass transfer rate.

AI.tldr: A relaxation-based, oscillation-free real-fluid finite-volume method is developed for the non-equilibrium flash-evaporation Riemann problem and used to show how finite mass- and heat-transfer relaxation times alter its wave structure.
AI.motivation: The equilibrium Flash evaporation Riemann problem (FeRP) cannot represent physical flash evaporation with finite-rate interphase heat and mass transfer, which causes the wave structure to deviate from the equilibrium state. A non-equilibrium Riemann formulation and a method for assessing thermodynamic relaxation effects are therefore needed.
AI.method: The paper derives the governing equation for mechanical equilibrium evolution in a relaxation system and develops an oscillation-free Homogeneous Relaxation Real Fluid (HRRF) finite-volume method. In addition to the Euler equations with mass relaxation, HRRF evolves advection equations for internal energy-pressure affine parameters and vapor volume fraction to eliminate numerical pressure oscillations while preserving phase-transition-induced pressure changes, and it degenerates to a completely pressure-equilibrium method in supercritical flows. HRRF is then used to evaluate how thermodynamic relaxation affects the FeRP solution.
