Compared with the equilibrium limit, a longer mass-transfer relaxation time smooths the expansion branch, lowers the intermediate pressure and velocity, and induces pseudo-splitting of the rarefaction wave and pseudo-advance of phase-transition onset. The heat-transfer relaxation time mainly controls the temperature difference in the vapor-liquid mixture, thereby modulating liquid superheat and the mass-transfer rate.
AI.conclusion: The HRRF method provides an oscillation-free real-fluid finite-volume framework that preserves phase-transition pressure changes and consistently reduces to a pressure-equilibrium method for supercritical flows. Applying it to the FeRP shows that finite mass- and heat-transfer relaxation times substantially modify the non-equilibrium wave structure and phase-transition behavior relative to the equilibrium limit.

title: Lensless single-pixel imaging through dynamic coded-aperture illumination
summary: We demonstrate a lensless single-pixel imaging (SPI) system combining dynamic coded-aperture illumination with single-pixel detection. Binary digital micromirror device (DMD) masks generate tailored grayscale intensity fields through coherent propagation, without relay projection optics or temporal grayscale synthesis. Six target-field configurations---uniform, Rayleigh speckle, squared-Rayleigh speckle, and sparse binary fields with $p=10\%$, $5\%$, and $1\%$---are evaluated using binary and grayscale objects. Intensity-correlation and nonnegative total-variation-regularized reconstructions reveal that the preferred illumination depends on the object, reconstruction method, and evaluation metric. By combining rapid binary modulation, programmable grayscale illumination, and single-pixel readout, this implementation provides a flexible architecture for lensless computational imaging and joint design of optical encoding and reconstruction.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates a lensless single-pixel imaging system that uses binary DMD masks to create programmable grayscale illumination through coherent propagation, then evaluates six illumination-field configurations with two reconstruction approaches on binary and grayscale objects.
AI.motivation: The work aims to provide a flexible lensless computational-imaging architecture that combines rapid binary modulation, programmable grayscale illumination, and single-pixel readout, enabling joint design of optical encoding and reconstruction.
AI.method: Binary digital micromirror device masks generate tailored grayscale intensity fields via coherent propagation without relay projection optics or temporal grayscale synthesis. Six target-field configurations are tested: uniform, Rayleigh speckle, squared-Rayleigh speckle, and sparse binary fields with p=10%, 5%, and 1%. Binary and grayscale objects are reconstructed using intensity correlation and nonnegative total-variation-regularized methods.
AI.result: The preferred illumination field depends on the object type, reconstruction method, and evaluation metric; no single configuration is reported as universally best.
AI.conclusion: The implementation offers a flexible architecture for lensless computational imaging and for jointly designing optical encoding and reconstruction.

title: Exact analytic anisotropic three-dimensional equilibria with nested magnetic surfaces, confined drift orbits and without spatial symmetry
summary: Exact toroidal fluid and kinetic equilibria with nested magnetic surfaces and no continuous symmetry are of great interest in laboratory, astrophysical and space plasmas. Their existence and stability have been open in physics and mathematics for decades. We construct such anisotropic-pressure equilibria by applying the Clemente transformation to exact vacuum fields. They connect smoothly to these fields on a fixed regular domain and preserve a regular magnetic axis, perfectly nested surfaces and spatially varying rotational transform. To our knowledge, the sheared configurations are the first exact anisotropic equilibria combining these properties with positive pressures and a positive firehose margin. The fixed-boundary Chew--Goldberger--Low (CGL) quadratic energy splits into a nonnegative vacuum-field term and a local pressure term, nonnegative for p_perp/p_parallel <= (3+\sqrt{21})/2 ~ 3.79. For p_parallel >= p_perp each configuration minimizes the finite-amplitude CGL energy over smooth boundary-fixed ideal material deformations. For the current-free configurations, physical guiding-center distributions produce these pressures within the same bound, with no free energy for magnetic-moment-conserving electrostatic perturbations. Trapped particles inherit the vacuum field's second adiabatic invariant at a rescaled magnetic moment, so local closed action contours carry over. The equilibrium code DESC reproduces them from the exact solution. Kinetic stability for surface-dependent rescalings and against general nonlinear electromagnetic perturbations remains open.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs exact three-dimensional toroidal anisotropic-pressure plasma equilibria with nested magnetic surfaces, a regular magnetic axis, spatially varying rotational transform, and no continuous spatial symmetry, by applying the Clemente transformation to exact vacuum fields. It derives CGL energy and stability properties, guiding-center pressure realizations, trapped-particle invariants, and numerical reproduction with DESC; some kinetic stability questions remain open.
AI.motivation: Exact toroidal fluid and kinetic equilibria with nested magnetic surfaces and no continuous symmetry are of broad interest for laboratory, astrophysical, and space plasmas, but their existence and stability have remained open in physics and mathematics for decades.
AI.method: The authors apply the Clemente transformation to exact vacuum fields to generate anisotropic-pressure equilibria on a fixed regular domain. They analyze the fixed-boundary Chew–Goldberger–Low (CGL) quadratic energy, its splitting into vacuum-field and local pressure terms, and minimization under smooth boundary-fixed ideal material deformations. They also relate current-free configurations to physical guiding-center distributions and reproduce the equilibria with the DESC code.
AI.result: The configurations preserve a regular magnetic axis, perfectly nested surfaces, and spatially varying rotational transform, and connect smoothly to vacuum fields on the domain. They are reported as the first exact anisotropic equilibria combining these properties with positive pressures and a positive firehose margin. The CGL energy is nonnegative for p_perp/p_parallel <= (3+sqrt(21))/2 ~ 3.79, and for p_parallel >= p_perp each configuration minimizes the finite-amplitude CGL energy over smooth boundary-fixed ideal material deformations. Current-free configurations have guiding-center pressure realizations within the same bound and no free energy for magnetic-moment-conserving electrostatic perturbations; trapped particles inherit the vacuum field's second adiabatic invariant at a rescaled magnetic moment, carrying over local closed action contours. DESC reproduces the exact solutions.
AI.conclusion: Exact anisotropic three-dimensional toroidal equilibria without continuous spatial symmetry can be constructed with nested surfaces, confined drift orbits, positive pressure, and favorable CGL stability properties under stated pressure-ratio and deformation conditions. Kinetic stability for surface-dependent rescalings and against general nonlinear electromagnetic perturbations remains open.

title: Cable construction effects on the lateral forces and wakes of helically stranded cables under oblique inflow
summary: Helically stranded cables in aerial towing systems experience oblique inflow, but are often modeled as smooth cylinders, neglecting three-dimensional cross-stream coupling and surface texture. We perform large-eddy simulations and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition for a smooth cylinder and four stranded cables at four inclinations from $22.5^\circ$ to $90^\circ$, all stationary, with $Re \approx 1.0 \times 10^4$. Aerodynamic differences are governed mainly by cross-sectional symmetry and strand-scale groove depth. Force-source decomposition shows that surface pressure contributes 94.9%--98.3% of the mean normal force and dominates the mean lateral force. High-symmetry, quasi-circular envelopes maintain balanced circumferential pressure, whereas deep-grooved, low-symmetry tri-lobed geometries produce asymmetric separation and a persistent lateral pressure imbalance. In the wake, high-symmetry cables sustain spanwise-synchronized Karman shedding at moderate-to-high inclinations, concentrating fluctuation energy in a dominant low-rank mode. Deep grooves disrupt shedding coherence, deflect the recirculation zone laterally, and spread energy across broadband scales. Mean lateral force and lateral-force fluctuations are therefore decoupled: the quasi-circular $(1 \times 19)$ cable has minimal mean lateral force but strong periodic fluctuations, while the deep-grooved $(3 \times 7)$ cable has weak fluctuations but appreciable mean lateral force. These results support construction-dependent cable selection and aerodynamic load modeling.

AI.tldr: Large-eddy simulations and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition compare a smooth cylinder with four helically stranded cables under oblique inflow, showing that cross-sectional symmetry and groove depth control lateral forces and wake organization.
AI.motivation: Helically stranded cables in aerial towing systems encounter oblique inflow but are often approximated as smooth cylinders, which neglects three-dimensional cross-stream coupling and surface texture.
AI.method: The study performs large-eddy simulations and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition for a smooth cylinder and four stranded cables at four inclinations from 22.5° to 90°, all stationary, with Re approximately 1.0 × 10^4. It also uses force-source decomposition to distinguish pressure and other contributions.
AI.result: Surface pressure contributes 94.9%–98.3% of the mean normal force and dominates the mean lateral force. High-symmetry, quasi-circular envelopes maintain balanced circumferential pressure, while deep-grooved, low-symmetry tri-lobed geometries produce asymmetric separation and persistent lateral pressure imbalance. High-symmetry cables sustain spanwise-synchronized Karman shedding at moderate-to-high inclinations, with fluctuation energy concentrated in a dominant low-rank mode; deep grooves disrupt shedding coherence, deflect the recirculation zone laterally, and spread energy across broadband scales. The quasi-circular (1 × 19) cable has minimal mean lateral force but strong periodic fluctuations, whereas the deep-grooved (3 × 7) cable has weak fluctuations but appreciable mean lateral force.
AI.conclusion: Mean lateral force and lateral-force fluctuations are decoupled and depend on cable construction. The findings support construction-dependent cable selection and aerodynamic load modeling.

title: Origin of devil's staircases and anomalous Arnold tongues of breathing solitons in optical Kerr resonators
summary: Synchronization phenomena are ubiquitous across natural and engineered systems, and optical resonators supporting breathing solitons offer a natural platform for their investigation. In driven Kerr cavities described by the Lugiato-Lefever equation (LLE), breathing-soliton dynamics constitute a minimal setting in which such behavior can be systematically analyzed. Despite recent observations of intricate self-synchronization structures in mode-locked lasers-such as subharmonic entrainment, devil's staircases, and holes within Arnold tongues, i.e., regions of unsynchronized dynamics embedded within synchronized domains-their physical origin has remained elusive due to the complexity of laser dynamics. Here, we demonstrate that these phenomena emerge in the universal framework of the LLE. By reducing the problem to this model, we uncover the mechanism responsible for both the devil's staircase and the formation of holes within Arnold tongues. This provides a unified physical picture of synchronization in nonlinear systems, extending beyond optics and providing insight into analogous predictions and observations in fluids and other oscillatory media. In addition, we identify the regimes of high-order synchronization, enabling the generation of ultradense frequency combs, opening new directions for precision photonic applications.

AI.tldr: The paper uses the Lugiato–Lefever equation to explain devil's staircases and anomalous holes inside Arnold tongues in breathing-soliton Kerr resonators, and identifies high-order synchronization regimes for ultradense frequency-comb generation.
AI.motivation: Synchronization is ubiquitous, and breathing solitons in driven Kerr cavities provide a minimal platform for studying it. Intricate synchronization structures observed in mode-locked lasers, including subharmonic entrainment, devil's staircases, and holes within Arnold tongues, lacked a clear physical explanation because of the complexity of laser dynamics.
AI.method: The authors reduce the breathing-soliton synchronization problem to the universal Lugiato–Lefever equation framework and analyze its synchronization structures, including Arnold tongues and high-order locking regimes.
AI.result: The authors demonstrate that devil's staircases and holes within Arnold tongues emerge within the LLE and uncover the mechanism responsible for both. They also identify regimes of high-order synchronization that enable ultradense frequency combs.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a unified physical picture of synchronization in nonlinear systems, extending beyond optics to analogous predictions and observations in fluids and other oscillatory media, while opening directions for precision photonic applications.

title: Self-organization of magnetic islands and zonal magnetic fields driven by slab microtearing modes in the absence of magnetic shear
summary: Self-organization in collisional microtearing turbulence is investigated using gyrokinetic simulations in a slab geometry without equilibrium magnetic shear. Unlike magnetically driven conventional tearing instabilities, microtearing instabilities are driven by the electron temperature gradient. Electron temperature fluctuations are found to contain most of the gyrokinetic free energy. Although magnetic perturbations contribute little to the free energy, the magnetic field structure plays a crucial role in the nonlinear evolution of microtearing turbulence. Zonal magnetic fields emerge spontaneously through the nonlinear interaction between magnetic perturbations and electron temperature fluctuations. These zonal fields provide an effective magnetic shear that enables magnetic islands to form despite the absence of equilibrium magnetic shear. The electron temperature profile is flattened within the islands. This flattening reduces the instability drive and is expected to promote turbulence saturation.

AI.tldr: Gyrokinetic slab simulations show that collisional microtearing turbulence without equilibrium magnetic shear self-organizes: nonlinear interactions generate zonal magnetic fields, whose effective shear allows magnetic islands to form and flatten the electron temperature profile, likely promoting saturation.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to understand self-organization in collisional microtearing turbulence in a slab geometry lacking equilibrium magnetic shear, distinguishing microtearing instabilities driven by the electron temperature gradient from conventional magnetically driven tearing instabilities.
AI.method: The authors use gyrokinetic simulations of collisional microtearing turbulence in a slab geometry without equilibrium magnetic shear.
AI.result: Electron temperature fluctuations contain most of the gyrokinetic free energy, while magnetic perturbations contribute little free energy but are crucial to nonlinear evolution. Zonal magnetic fields emerge spontaneously from nonlinear interaction between magnetic perturbations and electron temperature fluctuations, providing effective magnetic shear that enables magnetic islands to form despite the absence of equilibrium magnetic shear. The electron temperature profile is flattened within the islands.
AI.conclusion: The island-induced flattening of the electron temperature profile reduces the instability drive and is expected to promote turbulence saturation.

title: Reconstructing Interacting Blood Flow and Wall Interface Deformation from Noisy Flow Data Using PirateNets
summary: Blood flow and elastic vessel-wall motion interact with each other: fluid stress drives wall deformation, while the moving wall changes the domain in which blood flows. Given noisy flow images, we study the inverse problem of reconstructing the coupled, unsteady three-dimensional motions. We solve the reconstruction through Gauss--Seidel-type alternating fluid and geometry updates. For the fluid, we use physics-informed networks to recover velocity and pressure by fitting the observations while enforcing the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on the moving domain, which is described by an arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) map. For the geometry, a reference-domain correction and sequential registration recover the vessel shape and wall displacement. Interface traction continuity and an elastic momentum equation regularize the registration so that the recovered displacement is also physics-informed. The networks evaluate fields and physical residuals at sampled space--time points without remeshing the moving domain. Experiments on a converging channel and a patient-like aorta demonstrate reconstruction of flow and wall motion from noisy data. Ablation and parameter-sensitivity studies examine the role of structure regularization and imperfect physical coefficients. A further experiment with a three-element Windkessel outlet condition demonstrates how the framework accommodates a more physiologically realistic boundary setting.

AI.tldr: A Gauss–Seidel-type alternating framework combines physics-informed neural networks for ALE-described moving-domain Navier–Stokes flow with regularized sequential registration for vessel geometry to reconstruct coupled three-dimensional blood flow and elastic wall deformation from noisy flow images.
AI.motivation: Blood flow and elastic vessel-wall motion interact: fluid stress drives wall deformation, and the moving wall changes the flow domain. The paper aims to reconstruct these coupled, unsteady three-dimensional motions from noisy flow images as an inverse problem.
AI.method: The reconstruction alternates fluid and geometry updates in a Gauss–Seidel manner. For the fluid, physics-informed networks recover velocity and pressure by fitting observations while enforcing the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on a moving domain represented by an arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian map. For the geometry, a reference-domain correction and sequential registration recover vessel shape and wall displacement; interface traction continuity and an elastic momentum equation regularize the registration. Fields and physical residuals are evaluated at sampled space–time points without remeshing. Experiments include a converging channel and a patient-like aorta, ablation and parameter-sensitivity studies, and a three-element Windkessel outlet condition.
AI.result: Experiments on a converging channel and a patient-like aorta demonstrate reconstruction of flow and wall motion from noisy data. Ablation and parameter-sensitivity studies examine the role of structure regularization and imperfect physical coefficients. A further experiment with a three-element Windkessel outlet condition shows that the framework accommodates a more physiologically realistic boundary setting. The abstract does not report quantitative error values.
AI.conclusion: The proposed physics-informed alternating framework can reconstruct coupled blood flow and vessel-wall interface deformation from noisy images and can incorporate a Windkessel outlet condition. The reported studies support the utility of structure regularization and indicate sensitivity to imperfect physical coefficients; quantitative performance and broader validation are not provided in the abstract.

title: Wide Field 3D Color Topography for Large-Angle Structures
summary: Three-dimensional (3D) topography measurement is essential for industrial inspection and scientific research. However, existing techniques are limited by an inherent trade-off between resolution, speed, color imaging capability and the ability to measure large-angle surfaces. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel method that integrates ring light illumination based wide-field 3D imaging with an iterative shape-from-focus (SFF) algorithm. The system employs coaxial epi-illumination combined with ring light illumination to simultaneously acquire information from flat regions and steep slopes. The proposed iterative SFF algorithm achieves high-resolution 3D topography measurement. Full-color 3D reconstructions of electronic chips and PCBs demonstrate that the proposed method enables fast scanning and sub-micrometer resolution and significantly extending the measurable inclination range for large-angle structures. This method fills a critical gap in existing technology for fast, natural-color, 3D imaging and measurement of samples with steep topographies.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a wide-field, full-color 3D topography method combining ring-light illumination with an iterative shape-from-focus algorithm to measure large-angle structures at sub-micrometer resolution and high speed.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D topography techniques face an inherent trade-off among resolution, speed, color imaging capability, and the ability to measure large-angle surfaces, leaving a gap for fast, natural-color 3D imaging of steep topographies.
AI.method: The method integrates ring-light-illumination-based wide-field 3D imaging with an iterative shape-from-focus (SFF) algorithm. Coaxial epi-illumination combined with ring light illumination simultaneously acquires information from flat regions and steep slopes, while the iterative SFF algorithm reconstructs high-resolution 3D topography.
AI.result: Full-color 3D reconstructions of electronic chips and PCBs demonstrate fast scanning, sub-micrometer resolution, and a significantly extended measurable inclination range for large-angle structures. No further quantitative performance values are provided in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach fills a critical gap in fast, natural-color 3D imaging and measurement of samples with steep topographies by overcoming the usual resolution-speed-color-large-angle trade-off.

title: Magnetosonic Solitons Driven by a Moving Charged Source: Two-Fluid Modeling and PIC Validation
summary: We develop and validate a one-dimensional electron-ion two-fluid model, self-consistently coupled to Maxwell equations, for magnetosonic structures generated by a moving charged source. The model is independently benchmarked against kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations to assess its ability to reproduce electrostatic and electromagnetic responses. In the zero-magnetic-field limit, the electrostatic precursor structures are validated using the Korteweg--de Vries amplitude--width invariant. For a finite magnetic field, the frequency and propagation speed of the far wake are consistent with the low-frequency fast-magnetosonic branch, providing a linear benchmark for the electromagnetic response. The model reproduces the transition from a wake-dominated regime to localized forward precursors as the source velocity exceeds the magnetosonic speed, and to source-locked pinned structures at higher velocities. Independent PIC simulations recover the principal features of these regimes, supporting the validity of the two-fluid description for the parameters considered. By retaining separate electron and ion dynamics, electron inertia, and charge-separation effects, the validated model provides a framework for investigating source-driven plasma-wave structures across a broader range of plasma conditions and source-magnetic-field geometries, with potential applications to interpreting plasma-wave signatures associated with moving charged objects in space plasmas.

AI.tldr: The paper develops and PIC-validates a one-dimensional electron-ion two-fluid model coupled to Maxwell equations for magnetosonic structures driven by a moving charged source, reproducing electrostatic precursors, magnetosonic far wakes, and velocity-dependent wake-to-precursor transitions.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to establish and validate a self-consistent two-fluid framework for magnetosonic structures generated by a moving charged source, assessing whether it can reproduce electrostatic and electromagnetic responses independently benchmarked against kinetic PIC simulations.
AI.method: A one-dimensional electron-ion two-fluid model self-consistently coupled to Maxwell equations is developed. In the zero-magnetic-field limit, electrostatic precursor structures are checked with the Korteweg--de Vries amplitude--width invariant. For finite magnetic field, far-wake frequency and propagation speed are compared with the low-frequency fast-magnetosonic branch. The model is independently benchmarked against kinetic particle-in-cell simulations, retaining separate electron and ion dynamics, electron inertia, and charge-separation effects.
AI.result: The model reproduces the transition from a wake-dominated regime to localized forward precursors when the source velocity exceeds the magnetosonic speed, and to source-locked pinned structures at higher velocities. Independent PIC simulations recover the principal features of these regimes for the parameters considered, supporting the two-fluid description.
AI.conclusion: The validated two-fluid model provides a framework for investigating source-driven plasma-wave structures over broader plasma conditions and source-magnetic-field geometries, with potential use in interpreting plasma-wave signatures associated with moving charged objects in space plasmas.

title: Tuning fluid frictional drag through flow-induced aggregation of wormlike micelles
summary: Charged amphiphilic surfactants are versatile polymorphic molecules which can form supramolecular structures, such as wormlike micelles. We study the rheology and non-Newtonian fluid dynamics of the cationic surfactant trimethyltetradecylammonium chloride (TTAC) combined with the aromatic counter-ion sodium salicylate (NaSal). In the non-dilute regime, this solution exhibits a linear viscoelastic response consistent with a single-mode Jeffreys model, and in capillary pinch-off experiments, fluid filaments form extended cylindrical threads, indicating strong strain-stiffening. In the dilute regime the linear viscoelasticity and extensional rheology become immeasurably small, but the TTAC/NaSal mixture develops flow-induced structures at high shear rates, as the result of an end-to-end concatenation of micelles produced by shear-induced flow alignment. These flow-induced structures augment both the measured viscosity and the viscous drag in laminar flows at high shear rates (by as much as 50 %). In turbulent Taylor-Couette flow, the flow-induced structures produce a sudden and dramatic destabilizing influence on the stable toroidal Taylor vortices, resulting in upwards of a 200 % enhancement in turbulent drag. However, with increasing Reynolds number, the turbulent flow transitions smoothly to a state of drag reduction, generating up to a 30 % reduction in fluid frictional drag but without the shear-induced degradation that plagues drag reduction strategies based on solutions of high molecular weight polymer, such as polyacrylamide. These results show that surfactants are a unique and effective modifier of fluid frictional drag in both laminar and turbulent flow regimes, capable of producing both significant levels of drag enhancement and drag reduction by tuning the composition and operating conditions.

AI.tldr: The paper studies TTAC/NaSal wormlike micellar solutions and shows that flow-induced micellar aggregation can tune frictional drag, increasing laminar viscous drag and turbulent drag at some conditions while producing turbulent drag reduction at higher Reynolds numbers without polymer-like shear degradation.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to understand and exploit the rheology and non-Newtonian fluid dynamics of charged amphiphilic surfactant systems, specifically whether flow-induced structures in wormlike micellar solutions can serve as effective modifiers of fluid frictional drag in laminar and turbulent regimes.
AI.method: The rheology and non-Newtonian fluid dynamics of the cationic surfactant trimethyltetradecylammonium chloride (TTAC) with the aromatic counter-ion sodium salicylate (NaSal) were studied. The authors used linear viscoelastic measurements, capillary pinch-off extensional experiments, laminar flow viscosity and drag measurements, and turbulent Taylor-Couette flow experiments across dilute and non-dilute regimes and varying Reynolds numbers.
AI.result: In the non-dilute regime, the solution showed linear viscoelasticity consistent with a single-mode Jeffreys model and strong strain-stiffening with extended cylindrical threads in capillary pinch-off. In the dilute regime, viscoelasticity and extensional rheology were immeasurably small, but high shear rates produced flow-induced structures via end-to-end concatenation of shear-aligned micelles. These structures increased viscosity and laminar viscous drag by as much as 50%. In turbulent Taylor-Couette flow, they destabilized stable toroidal Taylor vortices and enhanced turbulent drag by upwards of 200%; at increasing Reynolds number, the flow transitioned smoothly to drag reduction of up to 30% without the shear-induced degradation typical of high-molecular-weight polymer drag reducers such as polyacrylamide.
AI.conclusion: Surfactant wormlike micellar systems are unique and effective modifiers of fluid frictional drag in both laminar and turbulent flow, capable of substantial drag enhancement and drag reduction through tuning composition and operating conditions, with the advantage of avoiding shear-induced degradation that limits some polymer-based drag-reduction strategies.

title: Three-dimensional polarization of thermal fields at arbitrary distances from thin-film emitters
summary: Recent advances have shown that thermal radiation can exhibit strong polarization in both the near and far fields. However, most existing studies focus on paraxial far-field emission, where polarization can be described using conventional two-dimensional (2D) Stokes parameters. Non-paraxial thermal radiation, with three nonzero vector components, requires a fully three-dimensional (3D) polarization description. This work develops a generalized theoretical method for analyzing thermal-radiation polarization at arbitrary distances from an emitter. Fluctuation-dissipation theory is employed to determine the $3\times3$ coherence matrix of the thermally emitted electromagnetic field, from which generalized 3D Stokes parameters are obtained. This method is applied to planar slabs composed of isotropic, anisotropic, and nonreciprocal materials. The results reveal distinct polarization behavior across the near- and far-field regimes. Near-field polarization is strongly influenced by evanescent waves and polariton dispersion, whereas far-field polarization is primarily governed by polarization-dependent radiative properties, including differences between transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) emission. Slab thickness further modifies polarization by controlling supported modes and interference effects. In addition, circular polarization, which vanishes in reciprocal slabs, is observed in n-type doped InAs under an external magnetic field that breaks reciprocity. This work provides a unified framework for characterizing the polarization of thermal electromagnetic fields from the extreme near field to the far field.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a generalized theoretical framework for describing the full three-dimensional polarization of thermal radiation at arbitrary distances from thin-film emitters, using a 3×3 coherence matrix and generalized 3D Stokes parameters. It applies the method to isotropic, anisotropic, and nonreciprocal planar slabs and shows distinct near-field, far-field, thickness-dependent, and magnetic-field-induced circular polarization behavior.
AI.motivation: Most studies of thermal-radiation polarization focus on paraxial far-field emission, where conventional two-dimensional Stokes parameters suffice. Non-paraxial thermal radiation has three nonzero vector components and therefore requires a fully three-dimensional polarization description.
AI.method: The authors employ fluctuation-dissipation theory to determine the 3×3 coherence matrix of the thermally emitted electromagnetic field and derive generalized 3D Stokes parameters from it. They apply the method to planar slabs made of isotropic, anisotropic, and nonreciprocal materials.
AI.result: The results show distinct polarization behavior in the near- and far-field regimes. Near-field polarization is strongly influenced by evanescent waves and polariton dispersion, while far-field polarization is primarily governed by polarization-dependent radiative properties, including TE and TM emission differences. Slab thickness modifies polarization by controlling supported modes and interference effects. Circular polarization, absent in reciprocal slabs, appears in n-type doped InAs under an external magnetic field that breaks reciprocity.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for characterizing the polarization of thermal electromagnetic fields from the extreme near field to the far field. Specific quantitative material parameters and experimental validation are not provided in the abstract.

title: GUERNICA: A continuum kinetic code for neutral dynamics in fusion plasmas
summary: We introduce GUERNICA, a GPU-accelerated continuum kinetic code for atomic hydrogen transport in fusion edge plasmas. It solves the Boltzmann equation with charge exchange, ionization, recombination and elastic neutral-neutral collisions. GUERNICA discretizes two-dimensional configuration space with the discontinuous Galerkin method on unstructured meshes and velocity space with the discrete velocity method in three dimensions, enabling direct simulation of the neutral distribution function without statistical noise. Unlike Monte Carlo methods, which introduce statistical noise and become computationally expensive in strongly collisional regimes, GUERNICA provides a deterministic alternative. An FFT-based evaluation of the full charge exchange operator reduces its computational complexity from $O(N_v^2)$ to $O(N_v \log N_v)$, enabling computationally practical simulations in three-dimensional velocity space. We verify GUERNICA against analytic tests and validate it against one-dimensional Monte Carlo results from DEGAS2. The numerical tests demonstrate the expected convergence orders and discrete conservation properties, while the DEGAS2 comparisons show agreement in neutral density and temperature to within 1.6%. Performance studies confirm the expected scaling of the FFT-based charge exchange operator and demonstrate efficient execution on a single GPU. Finally, we demonstrate GUERNICA in two dimensions using a static plasma background from a MAST-U SOLPS-ITER simulation, with $8.6\times 10^8$ phase-space degrees of freedom on a single GPU, illustrating the method's ability to resolve neutral dynamics in experimentally relevant divertor conditions.

AI.tldr: GUERNICA is a GPU-accelerated continuum kinetic code for atomic hydrogen transport in fusion edge plasmas. It solves the Boltzmann equation deterministically using discontinuous Galerkin discretization in two-dimensional configuration space, a three-dimensional discrete velocity method, and an FFT-based charge exchange operator. It is verified analytically, validated against DEGAS2 to within 1.6%, and demonstrated on a MAST-U SOLPS-ITER plasma background with 8.6×10^8 phase-space degrees of freedom on one GPU.
AI.motivation: Monte Carlo neutral transport methods introduce statistical noise and become computationally expensive in strongly collisional regimes, motivating a deterministic, noise-free alternative for simulating neutral distribution functions in fusion edge plasmas.
AI.method: GUERNICA solves the Boltzmann equation including charge exchange, ionization, recombination, and elastic neutral-neutral collisions. It uses discontinuous Galerkin discretization on unstructured meshes for two-dimensional configuration space and the discrete velocity method in three-dimensional velocity space. An FFT-based evaluation of the full charge exchange operator reduces complexity from O(N_v^2) to O(N_v log N_v).
AI.result: GUERNICA reproduces expected convergence orders and discrete conservation properties in analytic tests and agrees with one-dimensional DEGAS2 Monte Carlo results in neutral density and temperature to within 1.6%. Performance studies confirm the expected FFT-based charge exchange scaling and efficient single-GPU execution. A two-dimensional demonstration uses a static MAST-U SOLPS-ITER plasma background with 8.6×10^8 phase-space degrees of freedom on a single GPU.
AI.conclusion: GUERNICA provides a deterministic, GPU-accelerated alternative to Monte Carlo neutral transport simulation and can resolve neutral dynamics in experimentally relevant divertor conditions.

title: Reaching separated flow states by release and recapture with learned latent feedback
comment: 11 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to the Journal of Fluid Mechanics
summary: Targeting a prescribed flow configuration rather than an aerodynamic coefficient is challenging because the desired state may lie outside the natural attractor. We demonstrate cluster-based control in a learned vorticity representation for two-dimensional flow over a NACA0015 airfoil at $Re=500$ and $α=15^\circ$, using a localized streamwise momentum source near the leading edge. An actuation-enriched ensemble is compressed with a variational autoencoder and partitioned into macrostates. We optimize a continuous feedback law interpolating macrostate-dependent amplitudes without an explicit latent dynamical model. For an attached target, the optimized law approaches constant forcing, arrests vortex shedding and maintains the attached state. For a strongly separated target, the law instead establishes attachment, withdraws actuation so that the natural separation transient carries the flow through the target, and restores forcing to recapture attachment. Over the evaluation horizon, the closed-loop trajectory revisits the target approximately every three shedding periods. Companion open-loop calculations isolate the arrest, release and recapture processes.

title: Wavelength-resolved polarization characterization of supercontinuum vector beams
summary: The polarization state of a supercontinuum (SC) vector beam provides a reference for quantitative polarimetry. Attributing the measured boundary shift to this mechanism requires an intensity extinction ratio of about 7 or less at 766 nm if the offset at 450 nm is negligible and the shift corresponds to a uniform azimuthal angle change. title: Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
summary: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equation on the cubic torus with a constant odd-viscosity operator given by the vertical derivative of the curl. In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. title: Comments on: "Optimized thermal control of a dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavity"
summary: This comment addresses the publication [Appl. Opt. 65, 7090 (2026)] which targets an alleged ``optimization'' of a patented invention conceived by the author. The invention had introduced a multi-temperature management scheme for a dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavity that optimized the crystal temperature around the beam waist for phase-matching, while utilizing independently adjustable temperatures in other regions of the same crystal to simultaneously satisfy the double-resonance condition. A foundational form of this invention was initially utilized by co-author H. Vahlbruch without the author's prior knowledge during the construction of the squeezed-light laser for the Virgo gravitational wave detector. In their publication, the three authors now propose a variant that reduces the maximum achievable temperature differential. Here, I demonstrate that this approach does not constitute an optimization but, on the contrary, represents a regression that dismantles the invention. In general, a high-quality implementation of this invention fundamentally depends on maximizing the achievable temperature differential. Only then can the problematic phase differences---introduced by dielectric coatings, Gouy phase shifts, and suboptimal poling lengths at the crystal facets---be effectively compensated for, particularly in short crystals. If desired, smaller temperature differences can always be selected dynamically anyway.

AI.tldr: This comment disputes a claimed optimization of thermal control in a dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavity, arguing that the proposed variant reduces the achievable temperature differential and therefore regresses from the original invention rather than improving it.
AI.motivation: The paper responds to a publication that presents a variant of the author's patented multi-temperature management scheme for a dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavity as an optimization. The comment aims to defend the original invention, which independently adjusts crystal temperatures to satisfy phase matching near the beam waist and double resonance elsewhere, and to correct the characterization of the new variant.
AI.method: The abstract describes a conceptual and technical comment rather than an experimental study. It compares the proposed variant with the original multi-temperature management scheme and argues from the requirements of phase matching and double resonance, emphasizing compensation of phase differences caused by dielectric coatings, Gouy phase shifts, and suboptimal poling lengths at crystal facets. No quantitative modeling or experimental data are reported in the abstract.
AI.result: The comment concludes that the proposed approach does not constitute an optimization but is a regression that dismantles the invention because it reduces the maximum achievable temperature differential. It states that high-quality implementation fundamentally depends on maximizing that differential, especially in short crystals, so that problematic phase differences can be compensated; smaller temperature differences can instead be selected dynamically when desired.
AI.conclusion: The proposed variant is judged incompatible with the original invention's optimization principle. The comment asserts that maximizing the achievable temperature differential is essential for effective compensation of phase errors in dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavities, while smaller differences remain optionally selectable during operation.

title: Numerical-Relativity Particle-in-Cell Simulations: Self-Gravitating Collisionless Matter in Dynamical Spacetimes
summary: Gravitational collapse and instability, black-hole dynamics in systems with large scale separations, and questions surrounding extremal black hole formation require full nonlinear studies using accurate and adapted numerical tools. To this end, we present a new algorithm to study collisionless relativistic systems using a fully kinetic description of matter coupled to the evolving spacetime. In detail, we present a numerical-relativity particle-in-cell (NRPIC) framework for solving the Einstein--Vlasov system in three spatial dimensions. Implemented on top of the performance-portable \texttt{AthenaK} code, the method couples particle dynamics to Z4c spacetime evolution in moving puncture gauge through conservative stress-energy deposition on adaptively refined meshes. Our implementation makes use of advances in the computational modeling of relativistic plasmas using modern PIC models, now made available to general-relativistic gravity via an equivalent electrodynamic formulation. We introduce a Boris-type particle pusher that exploits the electrodynamic (Lorentz force) form of the geodesic force. We validate the coupled evolution against spherical dust collapse, follow prolate collapse through collisionless caustics into black-hole formation, and investigate the stability and nonlinear migration of relativistic clusters. Highlighting its potential to study gravitational instability in NR, we simulate the collapse of two overdensities within a common collisionless envelope, following black-hole formation, binary inspiral and merger, and subsequent mass accretion onto the remnant.

title: Amortized Transport-Map Likelihoods for Hierarchical Inverse Problems with Application to Wetting
summary: Hierarchical Bayesian models pool measurements, but with the forward model in the likelihood every posterior evaluation costs one forward solve per cell. To reduce this cost, we introduce a simulation-based inference framework in which a triangular transport-map likelihood, trained once per design, serves every cell. We apply it to infer wetting properties from photographs of a stable hole in a thin liquid film. The hole's radius depends, through the nonlinear Young-Laplace equation, on the contact angle and capillary length. One photograph gives rank-one information about them, so we pool many in a hierarchical model whose cells, each a substrate at one volume setting, share the apparatus geometry and the noise scale. A design fixes the number of substrates, the volume settings and the photographs per cell. The map's posteriors agree with direct sampling of the forward model in the wetting properties at a synthetic validation design, and less closely at a larger synthetic scaling design. At the validation design, simulation-based calibration detects no departure for any parameter. There, the map needs several hundred times fewer forward-model evaluations than direct sampling with a gradient-free ensemble sampler for a single posterior, and about five orders of magnitude fewer over a calibration study of 200 posteriors. On real photographs its posterior agrees with direct sampling and is consistent with the measured radii. Trained offline, the amortized map turns new photographs into a posterior with no forward solve. It is thus a major step toward measuring wetting properties in situ without disturbing the liquid.

Applied to photographs of holes in thin liquid films, it greatly reduces forward-model evaluations while agreeing with direct sampling at a validation design and on real data.

There, the map requires several hundred times fewer forward-model evaluations than direct sampling with a gradient-free ensemble sampler for a single posterior, and about five orders of magnitude fewer over a calibration study of 200 posteriors. title: Collective Chiral Response of Achiral Plasmonic Arrays Induced by Truncated Bloch-Floquet Effect
comment: 17 pages and 13 figures, including supplementary material. Plasmon polaritons, Chirality, Bloch-Floquet, Optical Angular Momentum, Metasurfaces
summary: Chirality in plasmonic systems is commonly associated with structures differentiated by their handedness. Here, we demonstrate the emergence of collective chirality in structurally achiral periodic hole arrays induced by non-local surface-plasmon interactions. We attribute this effect to the transfer of the optical angular momentum in the system. While an individual sub-wavelength circular aperture is not expected to alter the total angular momentum, the periodic structure results in a coherent coupling of plasmons wavefronts, giving rise to a collective Bloch-Floquet-like response. The edge of the structure accumulates the helical phase that eventually results in a visible spin-dependent shifting of the plasmonic beam. We systematically study the effects of hole-array size, periodicity and the geometry. The observed phenomenon shows an unprecedented robustness and consistency. These results establish periodic plasmonic arrays as a platform for converting localized helicity-dependent responses into collective chirality, providing a route toward controlling chiral plasmonic wavefronts in structurally achiral systems.

AI.tldr: Structurally achiral periodic plasmonic hole arrays exhibit collective chirality from non-local surface-plasmon interactions and a truncated Bloch-Floquet-like response, producing spin-dependent plasmonic beam shifts.
AI.motivation: Chirality in plasmonic systems is commonly linked to geometrically handed structures; this work investigates whether collective chiral responses can emerge in structurally achiral periodic systems.
AI.method: The authors study periodic sub-wavelength hole arrays and attribute the effect to transfer of optical angular momentum, coherent coupling of plasmon wavefronts, and a collective Bloch-Floquet-like response in which the structure edge accumulates helical phase. They systematically examine hole-array size, periodicity, and geometry.
AI.result: The arrays show a visible spin-dependent shifting of the plasmonic beam, with the phenomenon reported as unusually robust and consistent across the studied parameters.
AI.conclusion: Periodic plasmonic arrays can convert localized helicity-dependent responses into collective chirality, offering a route to control chiral plasmonic wavefronts in structurally achiral systems.

title: CoilStellaration: A Dataset and Benchmark for Engineering-Aware Stellarator Coilset Generation
comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Track on Evaluations and Datasets
summary: Stellarators are fusion devices that use externally generated, three-dimensional magnetic fields to confine hot plasma and offer a promising route to commercial fusion. Their electromagnetic coils pose a challenging design problem: they must reproduce the target magnetic field while satisfying engineering constraints and remaining practical and cost-effective to manufacture. Finding suitable geometries is a highly nonlinear inverse problem that generally has neither a closed-form nor a unique solution. This problem lies at the heart of stellarator design. We introduce CoilStellaration, a dataset and benchmark for learning the mapping between coil geometries from target plasma magnetic fields and engineering requirements. The dataset contains 177,000 optimized filamentary coilsets targeting plasma equilibria from ConStellaration, with sampled engineering requirements and achieved geometric and magnetic-field metrics. It spans multiple coil counts and field-period numbers, supporting studies of both specialized and shared models across configurations. The benchmark asks models to predict coils conditioned on a target equilibrium and requirements on coil-coil and coil-plasma spacing, curvature, and magnetic-field error. We show that magnetic-field accuracy remains the main challenge, with learned models rarely satisfying all requirements simultaneously. However, using learned predictions to initialize conventional coil optimization can accelerate early progress. We release baseline models and evaluation code to support reproducible research on both direct coil generation and learned optimization initializations. By lowering the barrier for machine learning and optimization researchers to engage with stellarator coil design, we aim to accelerate progress toward practical, cost-effective stellarator power plants.

title: Odd Darcy Law: Odd Viscosity and Edge Currents in Porous Media
summary: We derive and numerically validate an odd Darcy law for chiral active fluids in porous media, in which an antisymmetric permeability tensor induces a flow transverse to the applied pressure gradient. We then show how the transverse transport depends on porosity, boundary friction, and chirality.

title: A reachability criterion for spectrally factorable SPDC in coupled waveguides without periodic poling
comment: 32 pages, 9 figures, 11 tables; includes Appendices A-J
summary: Producing spectrally pure photon pairs by spontaneous parametric down-conversion without periodic poling would broaden the choice of nonlinear materials. It requires optical modes that provide both phase matching and suitable group velocities. We derive a joint reachability criterion for a constant-cross-section coupler with a nonlinear main guide and a linear auxiliary. In a two-mode description, phase closure fixes the hybridization parameter that also determines the main-guide participation and the attainable group-delay ratio. This relation screens material and mode pairs and specifies detuning and participation targets for full-vector refinement. A first-order purity map connects the reachable delay ratio and bandwidth--length product to the photon-pair spectrum. A full-vector AlN/TiO$_2$ feasibility example satisfies direct phase matching with a ratio of pump--idler to pump--signal group-delay mismatches of $-0.899$ and yields a calculated unfiltered Schmidt purity of 0.789 over 5 mm. The criterion links phase closure, dispersion control, and nonlinear participation when assessing coupled-waveguide sources beyond periodically poled materials.

title: Deriving Tsallis Entropy from First Principles
summary: The kinetic approach for q-distribution is extended through a "bottom-up" procedure to the corresponding entropic formula. In this way, the validity of Tsallis' formula, S_q(W) = k_B ln_q(W), is established from first principles. The resulting q-entropy is additive and the zeroth law of thermodynamics is automatically satisfied because the conventional identification beta = 1/(k_B T) remains valid. Entropy, energy, and all relevant quantities for both discrete and continuous cases are evaluated using standard (linear) averages. The "bottom-up" and "top-down" approaches yield the same q-distribution for velocities. The standard results are naturally recovered in the limit q -> 1.

title: A new approach to measuring both the steady flow curve and the planar extensional viscosity of complex fluids using exponential shear
summary: We revisit the protocol known as Exponential Shear (ES), first proposed by Doshi and Dealy in 1986. This is a transient strong flow that can be readily imposed in the laboratory using commercial strain-controlled (separate motor and transducer) rheometers which accurately measure both the (exponentially) time-varying torque and normal force exerted by the sample. Numerous studies over the years have proposed competing definitions of an appropriate material function for reporting data obtained from the exponentially time-varying imposed deformation. We revisit this unresolved challenge and carefully reconsider the exponential material kinematics involved and the proper definition of the corresponding material functions. We show that by understanding the time-varying eigenvalues and eigenvectors of both the shearing kinematics and the evolving state of stress in the sample it is, in fact, possible to use an exponential shear test to quantitatively map out \textit{both} the full flow curve (of shear viscosity vs. shear rate) and the steady planar extensional viscosity curve as a function of deformation rate. These findings are supported by numerical simulations of a number of nonlinear viscoelastic constitutive models, asymptotic analysis, as well as experiments with several polymeric liquids.

AI.tldr: The paper revisits exponential shear (ES) rheometry and proposes a material-function framework that uses a single transient ES test to measure both the steady shear flow curve and the steady planar extensional viscosity of complex fluids.
AI.motivation: Exponential shear was introduced by Doshi and Dealy in 1986 as a transient strong flow that can be imposed in commercial strain-controlled rheometers, but competing definitions of the appropriate material function have left the interpretation of ES data unresolved. The authors aim to resolve this challenge and establish a quantitative framework for extracting useful material properties from ES measurements.

They analyze the time-varying eigenvalues and eigenvectors of both the shearing kinematics and the evolving stress state, and support the approach with numerical simulations of several nonlinear viscoelastic constitutive models, asymptotic analysis, and experiments on several polymeric liquids.

title: 2D polaritons for Squeezing and Shrinking Light
summary: Two-dimensional (2D) materials have emerged as an extraordinary platform for polaritonics, given their remarkable ability to confine light to deep sub-wavelength scales. However, as material thicknesses reach the nanometer limit, macroscopic electrodynamic models become inadequate for the description of light-matter coupling in 2D materials, leaving a significant gap in our understanding of 2D polaritons. In this work, we develop a comprehensive quantum microscopic framework that describes 2D polaritons through a general, scale-less Hamiltonian. Starting from the quantum properties of a polarizable 2D surface, we derive collective excitations and we identify both transverse electric magnetic modes existing outside the light cone. Our results demonstrate that these 2D systems facilitate a powerful synergy between extreme wavelength shrinking and intrinsic quantum squeezing of electric field quadratures. By establishing this theoretical roadmap, our work provides the essential architecture for controlling non-classical states of light at the nanoscale, opening new avenues for high-precision quantum sensing and the development of next-generation optoelectronic devices

title: Solar cycle variations of meridional flow and differential rotation in a non-kinematic dynamo model
comment: To appear in Solar Physics journal
summary: Flux transport dynamo models have emerged as the leading paradigm for explaining the observed solar cycle. However, most of these models are kinematic and axisymmetric. We develop a non-kinematic dynamo model by specifying large-scale flows, such as the differential rotation and meridional flow. Thus, our model does not require the $Λ$ effect or other parameterisations of turbulent transport to generate the large-scale flows; it only solves the fluctuating flows and thermodynamics. Our model is inherently 3D by construction, although it is currently operating in axisymmetric mode because the source for poloidal field generation (Babcock-Leighton $α$) is assumed to be axisymmetric. Our model reproduces solar-cycle variations in both the meridional flow and the differential rotation -- specifically, the torsional oscillation in some agreement with observations. The model naturally exhibits some variability in the solar cycle, even without incorporating stochastic fluctuations, offering a new methodology for modelling the non-kinematic solar dynamo in 3D.

In axisymmetric mode with a Babcock-Leighton alpha, it reproduces solar-cycle variations in meridional flow and differential rotation, including torsional oscillations in some agreement with observations, and shows cycle variability without stochastic forcing.

title: Parameterized Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Efficient Simulation of Embedded Microfluidic Chip Cooling
summary: Embedded microfluidic cooling is a promising technology for dissipating the intense heat generated by high-performance electronic chips. However, the design and optimization of such coolers impose prohibitive computational costs when using conventional numerical solvers. Here, we present a parameterized physics-informed neural network (PINN) as a deep learning framework for rapidly and accurately predicting the thermohydraulic performance of embedded manifold microchannels. By incorporating four geometric dimensions along with three spatial coordinates as the network inputs, the proposed model enables multiphysics prediction across a continuous design space. Remarkably, our predicted velocity and temperature fields differ from finite-element simulations by relative errors of only 8.1% and 5.6%, respectively, while reducing the computational time and cost by over four orders of magnitude. Key to this framework is a composite strategy combining geometric ansatz embedding, the SOAP optimizer, and a thermal-conductivity-based curriculum learning scheme, which helps overcome the convergence challenges inherent in training PINNs for complex three-dimensional flows. Notably, by leveraging a highly optimized JAX backend, the network achieves convergence on a single consumer-grade GPU in less than four hours. Our approach offers a physics-consistent, real-time surrogate model that can substantially accelerate innovations in advanced microfluidic cooling of future electronics.

title: Improving the convergence of coupled quasinormal-mode theory for optical resonators
summary: Quasinormal modes (QNMs) provide a rigorous framework for describing resonances in open optical systems, including radiative and material losses. Recent coupled-QNM theories use the modes of individual resonators to predict the resonances and optical responses of coupled systems, without relying on phenomenological coupling parameters. However, their accuracy can deteriorate when the resonators confine light weakly and radiate strongly, often requiring many modes to obtain reliable predictions. Here, we introduce a reformulation of coupled-QNM theory that substantially improves its accuracy when only a small number of modes of the individual resonators are retained. The approach builds on the same underlying QNM framework but treats the fields mediating the interaction between resonators differently, leading to a new expression for the coupling coefficients. Numerical comparisons show that this extended-domain formulation is particularly advantageous for resonators with strong ra-diative losses, enabling more efficient modeling of a broader range of coupled photonic sys-tems.

AI.tldr: The paper reformulates coupled quasinormal-mode (QNM) theory for open optical resonators to improve accuracy when only a few modes per resonator are retained, with particular benefit for strongly radiating, weakly confining resonators.
AI.motivation: Existing coupled-QNM theories predict coupled-system resonances and optical responses from individual resonator modes without phenomenological coupling parameters, but their accuracy deteriorates for weakly confining, strongly radiating resonators and often requires many modes for reliable predictions.
AI.method: The authors introduce an extended-domain reformulation of coupled-QNM theory that remains within the same QNM framework but treats the fields mediating inter-resonator interaction differently, yielding a new expression for the coupling coefficients. The approach is evaluated through numerical comparisons.

title: Ergotropy as distance from equilibrium
summary: We show that the ergotropy (a.k.a available energy) of a thermally isolated system is the $1$-Wasserstein distance between two energy probability density functions. Specifically, between the energy profile of the system state, and the energy profile of its associated passive state. We prove this for both classical and quantum systems, and illustrate it with examples. Our result formalises the intuition that ergotropy is a quantifier of distance from equilibrium

AI.tldr: The paper identifies ergotropy (available energy) in thermally isolated classical and quantum systems with the 1-Wasserstein distance between the energy probability density function of the system state and that of its associated passive state, thereby formalizing ergotropy as a measure of distance from equilibrium.
AI.motivation: The work aims to formalize the intuition that ergotropy is a quantifier of distance from equilibrium.
AI.method: The authors prove, for both classical and quantum systems, that ergotropy equals the 1-Wasserstein distance between two energy probability density functions: one from the system state and one from its associated passive state. They also illustrate the result with examples.
AI.result: Ergotropy of a thermally isolated system is shown to be the 1-Wasserstein distance between the energy profile of the system state and the energy profile of its associated passive state, with the identity proven classically and quantum mechanically and demonstrated through examples.
AI.conclusion: Ergotropy can be understood as a distance from equilibrium, and this interpretation is formally established through its equivalence to a 1-Wasserstein distance between energy probability density functions.

title: Conductance scaling in nanopore arrays: disentangling roles of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry
summary: The scaling of electrical conductance with the number of nanopores, $N$, in an array is of fundamental importance for applications in membrane separation and ion transport across biological membranes, and has been the subject of longstanding disagreement in the field. Combining finite element calculations with theory, we resolve this disagreement for pores with negligible surface charge by showing that two previously conflicting predictions are each correct in their own limiting reservoir geometry: cuboidal reservoirs commensurate with the interpore spacing, for which the conductance scales linearly with $N$, and infinite reservoirs, for which the scaling is sublinear in $N$ for closely spaced pores. We show the transition between these limits with increasing reservoir size and, for infinite reservoirs, we show that a simple analytical model from electrical contact theory is mathematically equivalent to an existing point-charge capacitance model for nanopore arrays and validate its applicability against finite element and method-of-moments calculations. Using this model, we derive a characteristic coupling length, $\ell_\mathrm{c,95}$, the interpore spacing at which the array conductance reaches $95\%$ of that of the same number of independent pores. $\ell_\mathrm{c,95}$ scales linearly with pore diameter $d$, and grows with $N$ as $\sim\log N$ for linear arrays and $\sim\sqrt{N}$ for square arrays, so that pore coupling persists to surprisingly large separations in large arrays. Our work provides a general framework for predicting nanopore array conductance as a function of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry, of importance to nanofluidics research and the targeted design of functional devices.

It derives a coupling length that grows with array size and provides a framework linking conductance to pore arrangement and reservoir geometry.

title: Nonlinear Optical Properties of MXenes for Photonic Applications
summary: MXenes - a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides, nitrides, and carbonitrides - have emerged as powerful nonlinear photonic materials owing to their metallic conductivity, ultrafast carrier dynamics, broadband optical response, and highly tunable surface chemistry. This Review provides the first comprehensive overview of the nonlinear optical (NLO) properties of MXenes and their growing impact on advanced photonic technologies. We discuss state-of-the-art synthesis strategies, from fluoride-based etching to molten-salt, electrochemical, and CVD-enabled routes, highlighting how structural quality and surface terminations govern optical behaviour. A detailed analysis of third-order nonlinearities including Kerr effects, two- and multi-photon absorption, saturable and reverse-saturable absorption, and harmonic generation is presented, supported by quantitative comparisons across MXene families. We further examine modelling approaches linking band structure to nonlinear response and survey application frontiers such as gas sensing, ultrafast lasers, all-optical limiters, and emerging photonic neural networks. Finally, we outline future research directions spanning material engineering, device integration, and quantum/nonlinear metasurface platforms. Together, these insights position MXenes as a transformative materials platform for next-generation nonlinear photonics and ultrafast all-optical information processing.

title: Online Imitation Learning for Stabilizing Vlasov--Poisson Plasmas
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 43 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables
summary: We study the problem of controlling instability in the Vlasov--Poisson plasma systems, a fundamental challenge for nuclear fusion control. Motivated by the partial observability of plasma states in practice, we investigate imitation learning algorithms that learn from a fully-observable expert controller, but operate under macroscopic measurements. We theoretically establish a separation between online and offline imitation learning --- even a small behavior cloning error leads to error compounding that exponentially amplifies instability over time. By way of contrast, the online imitation learning loss can polynomially control the stability of rollout trajectories. We then propose a DAgger-style algorithm that learns the stabilizing controller under partial observability. Simulation results on a 1D Vlasov--Poisson system demonstrate that our algorithm can effectively stabilize plasma instabilities over longer time horizons than behavior cloning.

Theory shows that even small behavior-cloning errors compound exponentially, whereas online imitation learning can polynomially control rollout stability. A DAgger-style algorithm is proposed and shown in 1D simulations to stabilize instabilities over longer horizons than behavior cloning.

title: Interception Focusing of Colloid Transport in Granular Porous Media
comment: Pages: 57. Figures: 6 in main manuscript plus 5 tables and 10 figures in Supporting Information. Submitted to Environmental Science & Technology
summary: Colloid transport and retention in environmental granular porous media underlie groundwater resource protection from, and remediation using, biological and non-biological nano- and micro-particles (colloids). During transport, colloids periodically intercept grain surfaces and translate along them at separation distances across several tens of nm corresponding to the secondary minimum between the opposing forces of longer-range of van der Waals (VDW) attraction and shorter-range electric double layer (EDL) repulsion. Relatively weak diffusive translation of colloids supports their continued translation in secondary minimum association until they are expelled to bulk fluid at rear flow stagnation zones on grain leeward sides. We herein show that this dynamic focuses colloids into a network of fluid streamlines (incomplete mixing lamellae) that enhances their subsequent likelihood of interception with downgradient grains, i.e., increases the so-called collector efficiency (typically denoted by Greek letter eta). Interception focusing of colloids in granular porous media explains well-observed outcomes of colloid transport under environmental conditions, including nonmonotonic nonexponential profiles of retained colloids and the non-Markovian nature of extended tailing of low colloid concentrations following initial elution. Interception focusing is a fundamental process that distinguishes colloids from solutes and renders inapplicable to colloids the assumption that is often invoked for solutes of complete pore scale mixing in granular porous media.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes interception focusing as a mechanism by which colloids transported in granular porous media are concentrated into incomplete-mixing streamline lamellae, increasing their probability of interception with downgradient grains and explaining nonmonotonic retention profiles and long non-Markovian tailing.
AI.motivation: Colloid transport and retention in environmental granular porous media are important for groundwater resource protection and for remediation using biological and non-biological nano- and micro-particles; the paper aims to explain observed colloid transport behavior that differs from solute behavior.
AI.method: The abstract does not report specific experimental, computational, or modeling methods. It presents a mechanistic explanation based on colloids periodically intercepting grain surfaces, translating in the secondary minimum between longer-range van der Waals attraction and shorter-range electric double layer repulsion, and being expelled at rear flow stagnation zones on grain leeward sides.
AI.result: This dynamic focuses colloids into a network of fluid streamlines described as incomplete mixing lamellae, enhancing subsequent interception with downgradient grains and increasing collector efficiency (eta). Interception focusing explains nonmonotonic, nonexponential profiles of retained colloids and the non-Markovian nature of extended low-concentration tailing after initial elution.
AI.conclusion: Interception focusing is a fundamental process distinguishing colloids from solutes and makes the complete pore-scale mixing assumption often invoked for solutes inapplicable to colloids in granular porous media.

title: Precision-informed Fourier compression of refractive index tomograms with voxel-wise error control
summary: Significance: Holotomography (HT) generates large refractive index (RI) volumes and time series, creating a need for compact storage with controlled numerical fidelity. Aim: We sought to reduce storage by directly encoding reconstructed three-dimensional RI volumes in Fourier space with voxelwise validation against an assigned error budget. Approach: Quantized Fourier coefficients represent volumetric structure, while spatial residual quantization uses a 1% safety margin without storing separate corrections for individual voxels. We evaluated cellular and organoid data, concurrent processing, and extensions to dielectric-tensor and absorption tomography. Results: At a budget of 0.0001 RI units, complete packets achieved compression ratios of 7.89-9.50 relative to float32 arrays and were 28-30% smaller than BitRound-Pcodec packets satisfying the same error limit. Concurrent processing reduced encoding and decoding wall times by factors of 5.14 and 4.81 without changing packets. The fixed margin passed all primary-budget tests but failed at one smaller budget in both precision-sweep inputs. Conclusions: Precision-informed volumetric Fourier coding reduces storage of holotomograms with verified voxel-wise fidelity at the primary budget, at additional computational cost.

It reports 7.89–9.50× compression versus float32 at a 0.0001 RI-unit budget, 28–30% smaller packets than BitRound-Pcodec, and faster concurrent encoding/decoding, though one smaller budget failed.
